title: George W. Bush Presidential Library: NSC and White House Press Office Records re: September 4, 2002 CBS News Report (David Martin) on Rumsfeld's 9/11 Notes and the NSA-Intercepted 9/11 Call to Georgia

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, and the Presidential Records Act, 44 U.S.C. §§ 2201–2209 (including § 2204(c)(1)), I request copies of records held by the George W. Bush Presidential Library concerning the White House and National Security Council (NSC) handling of a September 4, 2002 CBS News report by national security correspondent David Martin. The report described notes taken by aides to Secretary of Defense Donald Rumsfeld on September 11, 2001. It also described a call intercepted by the National Security Agency at about 9:53 a.m. that day, from a bin Laden operative in Afghanistan to a telephone number in the Republic of Georgia.

For context: 

An article about David Martin's investigation into the intercepted telephone call is still hosted by CBS and can be found online at the link below, with the mention of the telephone call to Georgia mentioned in the third paragraph:
https://www.cbsnews.com/news/plans-for-iraq-attack-began-on-9-11/

A recording of this episode of the CBS Evening News that featured David Martin's report is currently hosted by YouTube at the link below. The mention of the call is in the first few minutes of the report:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xMScjLDVO8E


1. Scope:

All textual and electronic records (emails, attachments, memoranda, press guidance including "if-asked" guidance, talking points, Q&As, briefing and gaggle preparation materials, press inquiry and call logs, phone message slips, and drafts) dated September 3, 2002 through September 10, 2002, inclusive, that were sent to, sent from, copied to, or maintained by:

a. The NSC Press Office and NSC communications staff, including the NSC spokesperson and director-level press staff, and any assistants or detailees, specifically including Anna M. Perez and Sean McCormack 

b. The White House Office of the Press Secretary, including Ari Fleischer, Scott McClellan and Claire Buchan, and the Office of Communications, including Dan Bartlett;

c. NSC European and Eurasian Affairs staff, including Daniel Fried and Matthew Bryza, to the extent they contributed to guidance on Georgia or the Pankisi Gorge; and

d. Condoleezza Rice and Stephen Hadley, limited to communications concerning press response to the CBS report.

Records are responsive if they contain any of the following terms in the subject line, body or attachments: "CBS"; "David Martin"; "Pankisi"; "Duisi"; "Georgia" or "Tbilisi" or "Shevardnadze" or "Menagarishvili" or "Japaridze" or "Ambassador Japardize" (each in proximity to "intercept," "NSA," "Afghanistan" or "9/11"); "Rumsfeld" in proximity to "notes," "Cambone" or "Iraq"; "Saddam" or "S.H." in proximity to "UBL," "9/11" or "September 11"; "sweep it all up"; "go massive."

I also request records reflecting any inquiry to NSA, CIA or the Department of Defense about the accuracy or sourcing of the CBS report, to the extent held in the files described above.

2. Context:

The CBS report ran on September 4, 2002, as the administration was making its public case on Iraq. I seek the internal communications, press inquiries and guidance created in the days before and after the broadcast.

3. Format, Review and Exemptions

Please provide records electronically as searchable PDFs. Release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b). For anything withheld, please provide an itemized description identifying each record and the exemption claimed. A logical assumption is that any material prepared for release to, or in response to question from, a member of the news media would be, by definition, not classified. However, if any responsive material is classified, please treat this letter as a request for mandatory declassification review under E.O. 13526 § 3.5. If any records or portions are referred to NSA, CIA or DoD for consultation, please notify me of the referral and the receiving agency.

I am an amateur researcher, and I intend to disseminate the results publicly, including through MuckRock. I am not requesting for commercial use. I ask that fees be waived under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(iii), because release would contribute significantly to public understanding of how the September 11 attacks and Iraq were presented to the public.

Thank you for the work that the George W. Bush Presidential Library does and thank you for the commitment to transparency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

title: Records Filed, Disclosed or Used in United States v. Kaleb Cole, No. 2:20-cr-00032-JCC (W.D. Wash.) (Executive Office for United States Attorneys)

communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Officer:
Under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I request the records described below concerning United States v. Kaleb Cole, No. 2:20-cr-00032-JCC (W.D. Wash.) This is a new, narrower request. It is not a duplicate of FOIPA No. 1763941-000. It names Joshua Sutter only because he testified publicly for the government, as its FBI informant, at the trial of Kaleb Cole (Dkt. 274 at 86–107).

Scope limits

This request is limited to records that were filed, disclosed or used in the prosecution of Kaleb Cole. It does not seek:
- the confidential source’s aliases, source number, contact information, address, location or biographical details beyond what he stated in open court at trial (Dkt. 274 at 86–107);
- the identity of any FBI personnel other than those already named in public court filings in this case;
- operational details of any ongoing investigation; or
- records of any other investigation.

Records requested

1. Public filings and exhibits. Copies in your possession of the search warrant application and affidavit dated February 24, 2020 (SA Casey M. Villarreal; S.D. Tex. No. H20-0391M; W.D. Wash. Dkt. 194-1), and any exhibit, declaration, transcript, recording or screenshot that the government filed on the public docket or presented in court in the Cole case that describes or relies on information from the confidential source, including Dkt. 261. Also Dkt. 200 (the government’s response), Dkt. 211 (the Court’s order), and the trial testimony and the publicly filed redacted versions of Exhibits 100–111 (Dkt. 274 at 24–26 and 86–107; Dkt. 257).

2. Compensation disclosures. The government's letters, discovery cover letters or other written disclosures to defense counsel, and any related internal summary, stating the compensation and expense payments made to the confidential source in connection with this investigation, including the figures quoted in Dkt. 194 at 2 and 8–9 ($78,133.20 and $4,378.60) and the total since 2003 stated there, which the government states at Dkt. 200 at 10–11 and the Court recites at Dkt. 211 at 4.

3. Government responses. The government's filings, declarations and correspondence responding to the defense's challenge to the February 24, 2020 affidavit, including its response to Dkt. 194 (Dkt. 200), to the extent they address the source's reliability or how the FBI attributed the Wire account referenced in the affidavit to Mr. Cole.

4. Corroboration records. Records sufficient to show how the FBI corroborated the information from the source that was used in the February 24, 2020 affidavit, limited to the portions that do not identify the source. See Dkt. 200 at 4 and 7–10, where the government describes that corroboration.

5. Trial and sentencing records. The government’s trial brief (Dkt. 212), exhibit lists (Dkt. 213, 228 and 246), sentencing memorandum (Dkt. 261), and the sentencing transcript (Dkt. 272), to the extent they refer to the source or to evidence derived from him.

Time period
February 7, 2018 through the present, limited to records connected to the Cole prosecution.

Exemptions and segregability
Most of the records above appear to be in the public record, so I ask that you process them first and release them. For any withheld portion, please release all reasonably segregable material, identify each exemption claimed for each record or portion, and explain the foreseeable harm under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8)(A). Because the source’s identity and FBI role were disclosed in open court at trial, I ask that you not issue a Glomar response without explaining why the public court record has not already acknowledged the facts at issue.

Third-party privacy
This request names Joshua Sutter, a third party, but only as to matters he and the government disclosed in open court. He testified under oath and by name as a government witness at the trial of Kaleb Cole, stating that he had worked as an FBI informant since 2004, had been paid more than $100,000, and had joined and reported on Atomwaffen at his FBI handler’s direction (Dkt. 274 at 86–107). An FBI special agent testified to the same history and pay (id. at 24–26), the Court’s trial witness list records the “Confidential Human Source” as having testified on September 28, 2021 (Dkt. 247), and the Ninth Circuit described his prior conviction and FBI compensation in affirming the conviction (Dkt. 281 at 3–4). Any privacy interest in information already disclosed in open court is minimal, and it is outweighed by the public interest in how the government used a paid informant in a federal prosecution, a question both the district court and the Ninth Circuit addressed (Dkt. 211 at 4; Dkt. 281 at 3–4). See DOJ v. Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, 489 U.S. 749, 772–75 (1989); Cottone v. Reno, 193 F.3d 550, 554–56 (D.C. Cir. 1999). I do not have a privacy waiver from Mr. Sutter, and I do not seek his tax, medical, family, financial or other non-public personal information. If you conclude that any portion must be withheld under exemption (b)(6) or (b)(7)(C), please release the segregable remainder and identify the specific privacy interest involved, rather than refusing to confirm or deny the existence of records about matters he disclosed publicly.

Please provide electronic copies, in native format where available. For audio or video, please provide the files themselves.

I am an independent journalist and I request these records as a representative of the news media under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(ii)(II) and 28 C.F.R. § 16.10(b)(6). I gather information of potential interest to the public, use my editorial skills to turn it into original reporting, and publish that reporting on my blog. I intend to publish and analyze the records I receive and I have no commercial interest in them. I ask for a fee waiver under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(iii) because disclosure is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the government's use of paid confidential informants in a federal prosecution. The records concern the operations and activities of the FBI and the Department of Justice. They have informative value because they would show how the government used a paid informant in a federal prosecution, a question both the district court and the Ninth Circuit addressed (Dkt. 211 at 4; Dkt. 281 at 3–4). I will make them available to a broad public audience through my blog. See 28 C.F.R. § 16.10(k). In the alternative, if a fee waiver is denied, I ask that you classify me as a representative of the news media, so that I am charged only duplication fees after the first 100 pages. 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(ii)(II), (iv). Electronic copies are preferred. If a waiver is denied, please contact me before incurring fees over $300.

If any part of this request is unclear or too broad, please contact me to narrow it before closing it.

Thank you.
Sincerely,
Oscar Cozza

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: APD Social Media Surveillance
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

Unless stated otherwise, this request covers records created, sent, received or in effect between January 1, 2020, and the date this request is processed.

Definition: "Social media monitoring software" means any software, platform, subscription or service used to search, collect, monitor, analyze, alert on or retain information from social media services (for example Facebook, Instagram, X/Twitter, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, Snapchat, Telegram or Discord). This includes, but is not limited to, products from: BrightPlanet, Babel Street, Cobwebs Technologies / Penlink (Tangles), Dataminr (First Alert), Fivecast, Geofeedia, Intrado, LifeRaft (Navigator), Magnet Forensics, Media Sonar, ShadowDragon, Signal Corporation, Skopenow, Social Links, Voyager Labs and ZeroFOX.

Because Magnet products are also used for phone and computer forensics, for Magnet Forensics this request covers only items 1, 2, 4 and 6 (procurement, product, policy and training records). I am not requesting case files, extraction reports or examination records for any device or individual.

1.  Procurement and payment. All contracts, agreements, quotes, purchase orders, invoices, subscription or license renewals, P-card or credit card transactions, and grant applications or awards (including any federal grant funds) for social media monitoring software.
2.  How the software works. Product descriptions, user manuals, capability statements, technical specifications and vendor presentations for any social media monitoring software APD uses or has used.
3.  Vendor communications. Emails and attachments between the vendors named above and whoever currently holds the following positions: the commanding officer of APD's Critical Intelligence Center (and any analysts assigned to it), the City IT staff responsible for APD technology projects (project manager and Deputy CIO), and the purchasing or grants staff who process APD technology purchases, that contain at least one of these terms: "contract", "quote", "invoice", "renewal", "pilot", "trial", "demo", "license" or "subscription". Please exclude automated marketing emails, newsletters, webinar invitations and any message containing the word "unsubscribe".
4.  Policies. All general orders, directives, SOPs, policies or guidelines that govern the use of social media monitoring software, including rules on authorization, permitted purposes, data retention and audits.
5.  Officer and undercover accounts. All policies, general orders or guidelines that govern APD personnel using personal, fictitious, alias or "undercover" social media accounts for investigative or intelligence purposes, and any approval forms or logs used to authorize such accounts.
6.  Training. All training materials, presentations and course records used to teach APD personnel how to use social media monitoring software or how to collect information from social media.
7.  Outside sharing. All agreements, MOUs, policies or logs that cover sharing information obtained through social media monitoring software with entities outside APD (including other law enforcement agencies, fusion centers and federal agencies).
8.  Configuration and audit records. Saved search terms, keyword lists, watchlist names or categories, geofence locations, alert settings, and any usage, audit or compliance reports for social media monitoring software. I am not requesting the social media content of any individual, and the City may redact names and personal identifiers under Section 7(1)(c).

Please provide records electronically (PDF, or native format for spreadsheets and logs) by email. If no responsive records exist for an item, please say so for that item.

If any part of these records is withheld or redacted, please cite the specific exemption under 5 ILCS 140/7 for each redaction and release all reasonably segregable, non-exempt portions.

If you believe any item is unduly burdensome, I ask that you contact me under Section 3(g) so we can narrow it before any denial.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. 

Sincerely,

M

communications.subject: Pennsylvania Right to Know Act Request: Cheltenham - Local Data Sharing
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Pennsylvania Right to Know Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting records concerning the Cheltenham Township Police Department’s participation in the LexisNexis Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC), a platform through which law enforcement agencies contribute records management and dispatch data to a shared national database.

1) The ""AVCC XML Addendum"" or ""Consortium Sub-Agency Agreement"" signed between your agency and LexisNexis Risk Solutions (also known as RELX, LexisNexis Risk Management, or Accurint). This is the document that indicates whether your agency’s RMS/CAD data is shared only with consortium members or shared nationally. Either document alone is sufficient for this item.

2) Invoices issued by LexisNexis Risk Solutions to your agency during the last twelve months (if you receive monthly invoices, we only need the most recent two) 

3) A document, typically a spreadsheet, showing which crime types are and shared with LexisNexis. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. A LexisNexis account administrator can produce it by opening ""Data Classification Manager"" under the admin permissions menu on the left-hand side and using the Export link at the top right of that page. Depending on which LexisNexis products your agency subscribes to, this report may have a different name or location. We are looking for the list of what data your agency shares, and who it is shared with. 

4) If your agency takes part in a different data sharing group (CrimeTracer, N-Dex, Linx, etc.) then please provide one contract, MOU, or other document per data-sharing group to help us understand which group(s) your agency shares local data CAD/RMS/JMS data with.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Axon Contract and Procurement Materials
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) is submitting this request for records under the Illinois Freedom of Information Act. related to the acquisition and cost of services and devices provided by Axon and any of its subsidiaries and partners. 

*Background*
Axon (also known as Axon Enterprise, Inc.) is a company that describes itself as providing “public safety technology solutions” to a variety of customers, many of which are law enforcement agencies based in the United States. For reference, Axon’s website is www.axon.com. These “solutions” may be equipment, software, or “artificial intelligence”-driven analysis of video and data. Some examples of equipment, software, and services created and sold by Axon include (but are not limited to):
• the TASER, a conducted energy device
• body-worn cameras (often referred to as “Axon Body”)
• Axon Fusus, a platform used to integrate cameras and other data into a “real-time crime center” (RTCC) 
• Axon 911, an AI-driven assistant platform for dispatchers
• Axon Evidence, a platform to integrate evidence and other information
• Axon Outpost, an automated license plate reader (ALPR) system
• Axon Lightpost, an ALPR system designed for integration with streetlights
• the Axon AI Era Plan, a collection of AI-driven analysis software (www.axon.com/products/axon-ai-era-plan)
• Axon Vision, an AI-driven video analysis system
• Axon Assistant, an AI-driven chatbot
• Axon Draft One, an AI-assisted police report generation feature
• Axon Records, a records management system
• Axon virtual reality training
• Axon Air DFR, a drone-as-first-responder platform, which may also include drones created by a company called Skydio

Axon provides services or devices to the majority of policing agencies in the United States. Axon often “bundles” services and devices into a single contract, makes adjustments and additions to existing agreements for the provision of new goods, and is designated a “sole source provider” during the procurement process. Contracts and agreements may be active for many years and may include “escalator” clauses that describe ongoing and increasing costs for the procurement over the life of the contract.

*Timeframe*
The requested records are all those related to agreements with Axon active during the year 2026, as well as those agreements related to devices, services, and payments to be provided in the future. 

*Requested records*
This public records request is for materials related to the acquisition and cost of services and devices provided by Axon and any of its subsidiaries and partners. 

1. CONTRACT AND AGREEMENTS
All contracts, memorandums of understanding, and any other written agreements between this agency and Axon. Response records included all associated amendments, exhibits, and supplemental and supporting documentation for each agreement, including any amendments and materials generated subsequent to the initial contract agreement. If this agency uses any Axon product, including but not limited to the ones listed above, agreements referencing those products are responsive to this request; this includes all agreements related to “trial” or “free” periods of use. 

2. FINANCIAL AND PROCUREMENT MATERIALS
All relevant procurement and financial documents and agreements, as well as records of financial transactions, exchanges, and obligations relevant to devices and services procured from Axon. Some of these details and documents may be included as part of the Master Services and Purchasing Agreement or related quotes. 
Responsive materials include: 
• quote materials
• invoices and bills
• records describing specific pricing for each associated line item, including the unit price, the quantity procured of each unit, and associated pricing components. If additional products will be procured over the life of the contract, please be sure to provide records that reflect future acquisitions under the agreement and their cost. 
• receipts
• Requests for Proposal to which Axon provided a response
• bidding materials provided by Axon
• justifications for sole source designation (or equivalent designation, if different terminology is used in your jurisdiction) and associated materials. Responsive materials include any letters and drafts provided by Axon, any supporting materials provided by the company, and any related resolutions and materials generated by the jurisdiction in the process of obtaining a sole source designation for Axon. If the company is not subject to competitive purchasing procedures for a reason that is not a “sole source designation” (for example, because the agreement is part of a cooperative or collaborative purchase), please provide records sufficient to show why the company or the contract is not subject to competitive bidding. 
• records sufficient to show the projected ongoing cost of the agreement with Axon
• records reflecting any discounts or other calculations that were figured into the costs associated with this procurement

*Provision of records*
We ask that these materials be provided on a rolling basis; please provide materials to us as your office collects and reviews records. Please contact us for further discussion regarding the search and release of these materials.

*Fees*
In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform us of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. 
This request is not being made for commercial purposes. Please assess fees appropriately in accordance with a public records request being made in the public interest for research and journalism purposes.

*Format of responsive records*
I request that all records be disclosed in their native, digital format and transmitted to us electronically. 

*Contact information*
If you need any more information in order to process the request, or cannot process a portion of the request for any reason, please respond to the email address on this request or “beryl@eff.org”. Please let us know if a phone call will be necessary or desirable; such contact information will be provided upon request.

Thank you very much for your time and help.

Sincerely,
Beryl Lipton

Matthew Petti
